groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–2 题
groups.material:
Everything changed for 7-year-old Tariq when he slapped some butter on an ear of corn. He knew it tasted good, but butter made it better. His passion for produce got him a position as South Dakota's official Corn Ambassador.
Tariq's profession of love for his favorite vegetable earned him the name "the Corn Kid". This was after his online interview attracted millions of views and was made into a song. South Dakota is one of the top corn producers in America. The corn provides nourishment across the globe. Tariq said, "Not everyone has to like corn, but everyone should definitely try it, especially with butter." Tariq and his family were invited to South Dakota to attend the honorary ceremony at the state's Corn Palace. Officials wanted to highlight South Dakota's two largest industries: tourism and agriculture. Tariq couldn't believe his eyes when he saw the palace made of corn.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 3–4 题
groups.material:
Two arrests were announced Thursday. The arrests were in connection with a string of mail thefts from U.S. Postal Service's collection boxes in Marion County and for the possession of a stolen postal key, according to the Department of Justice.
Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman, both 23, were arrested after evidence gathered in an investigation showed the pair stole mail on multiple occasions using a postal key, according to a news release.
Jax and Goodman stole mail for around four months. Investigators reviewed videos of the collection boxes; the video showed the two men loading the stolen mail into Jax's vehicle. Investigators were also able to recover the key that was used to open the collection boxes.
Jax and Goodman each face up to five years in federal prison in the mail thefts and up to ten years for possession of the postal key.

groups.title: Section A · 第 3 篇 · 5–7 题
groups.material:
Can fast-fashion be sustainable? Researchers think yes. Identifying why the fast-fashion business model creates waste and determining whether regulators can establish incentives for consumers and manufacturers are steps to reduce waste.
Recently, the clothing industry has come under attack for creating a waste problem with serious environmental consequences. In the absence of environmentally and economically feasible recycling options, fast-fashion manufacturers pump out low-quality clothes produced in high volumes that are worn only a few times and then discarded.
The researchers put forth policy contributions, ranging from sustainable disposal of leftover stock to production tax to incentivize both manufacturers and consumers to be more waste conscious.
In order to devise effective policies to curb the environmental impact of the clothing industry, it is important to identify the source of the problem in the supply chain. Manufacturers, consumers, and regulatory bodies can then take an informed approach to recognize the environmental impact of fast-fashion and to design an ecosystem to reduce waste, incentivize innovation, and create new business models to manage waste.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 8–11 题
groups.material:
M: Hey Mary, you seem to be very much annoyed. What happened?
W: Rush hour in this city is killing me.
M: Ah, yes. Rush hour is terrible, especially in the morning between 8 and 9. But what else can you expect in a city this big?
W: Well, I think the local government could help improve things. I mean, getting rid of rush hour may be impossible, but it could be made more tolerable, don't you think?
M: Um… but I'm not sure how.
W: Well, for example, the subway system could have air conditioning. I know many cities in the world have air conditioning in their subway, so why can't we? It gets so hot in the summer. I can hardly breathe down there. And add to that the rush-hour crowds with strangers packed close together in the subway carriages, the whole thing is just horrible.
M: Ah, yes, you are completely right. The trains here are too old. The government should definitely invest in new ones with air conditioning. I guess I'm fortunate I take the bus instead.
W: Oh, that's much better.
M: Yeah, it's more convenient. Bus No. 36 goes straight from my house to the office. It's a 30-minute ride and I don't have to make any changes.
W: That sounds nice. I tell you, my current commute is killing me. Maybe I should move closer to the office.
M: Well, I know a great housing agent. I found the flat I'm living in now through him. And I love it.
W: Hmm, could you send me his number, please?
M: Sure thing. Just tell him exactly what you are looking for and I'm sure he will find something good.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
M: Did you hear about Johnny?
W: No. Why? Is he okay?
M: He had some plastic surgery done.
W: What? Why?
M: Do you remember he had a scar on his face?
W: Yes, of course. He always had that. I've known him since primary school, and I always remember him having that on his cheek.
M: Well, he had it fixed.
W: Fixed? What do you mean? You can't fix a scar.
M: You know what I mean? He had an operation done on it, plastic surgery, in order to cover it and make it less noticeable.
W: Oh, well, that's ridiculous, isn't it? It was noticeable, sure. But it wasn't an ugly scar. It never occurred to me that he should have it taken care of like that.
M: I agree. I can understand some scars and physical defects can be ugly and distracting, but not Johnny's. In fact, I thought it added character… like it gave him a certain uniqueness.
W: He must have felt differently though. He must have felt self-conscious and insecure, perhaps.
M: No, no, that's not the reason. He was totally fine with his scar. As you said, he had had it for most of his life.
W: Then why did he have the operation?
M: Because his girlfriend wanted him to.
W: What? That's so superficial and selfish of her. If Johnny's girlfriend doesn't like him for who he is, then she does not deserve to be his girlfriend.
M: You are right. So he is insane to give in to her like that. But when I told him, he said he loves her and would just do what she wants him to.
W: What a fool he is.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
Talking is unique to humans. An animal might make 10 different sounds, but an adult human knows more than 20,000 words. Additionally, we're the only animal that expresses thoughts in full sentences. Researchers don't think language was invented; instead, they think it evolved. How did talking evolve? There are two main theories.
The first theory is that language started with people making different sounds, mostly imitating the things around them, like animal calls, nature sounds, and the sounds of tools. Perhaps they made the sound of wind to comment on the weather or imitated the sound of a bird to tell a friend that there was a bird nearby. Then over hundreds of thousands of years, those sounds turned into words that people began to learn as part of their language. At some point, people started stringing the words together to form sentences.
The other main theory, which is more recent, is that people started off by gesturing—pointing at things with their hands and imitating actions using their bodies. Eventually these gestures turned into a full sign language. This theory guesses that after developing sign languages, people eventually started making sounds along with their gestures. At some point, they switched to mostly making sounds that became words instead of just using their bodies. The reason they switched to making sounds, the theory goes, is that talking out loud lets you communicate with someone even when you can't see them.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
Is it a good idea to display luxury brands and other signals of status? It depends on the situation. Studies have shown that people who appear to be wealthy tend to be considered more intelligent, disciplined, and competent than those who do not. But new research found that people believe someone who shows off their social status cares more about benefiting themselves than helping others. This means people are less willing to collaborate with them. Modesty may be key when cooperation is essential, but the researchers also found that in some cases, status signaling has advantages.
Experiments showed that participants were less likely to choose someone who signals their wealth or status to join a group seeking cooperative members. But participants were more likely to choose that person when they're looking for a competitive team member. These findings suggest that people should change how they present themselves depending on their social goal.
This is the era of social media. People can easily share their wealth and status to large audiences, but they need to consider the consequences. Posting about luxury purchases and expensive vacations online may help you to persuade others and frighten competitors, but it could also signal to potential friends or future employers that you are unlikely to think about the needs of others. This makes things tricky for people who may want to impress others while also demonstrating that they are a team player.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Human fascination with animals goes back as far as humans do. Of the oldest cave paintings discovered, some are up to 40,000 years old, and there are more images of animals than humans. At some point, humans began to capture and hold animals.
The first-known collections were held by royalty and were not open to the public. In Egypt, researchers have found buildings from around 3500 B.C., containing the remains of animals, including elephants, which were not native to Egypt. But life wasn't easy for these animals. They probably had short lives, and their remains show evidence of severe injuries.
The first public exhibit of animals may have been created by Egypt's Queen Hatshepsut around 1480 B.C. Researchers think the zoo was started with animals brought home from a far-off land known as Punt. It's unclear why the Queen built the zoo, but it might have been to show off her wealth and power.
Early zoos are found all over the world. In China, Emperor Wenwang is said to have built a "Garden of Intelligence" around 1060 B.C. It included deer, birds, and many fish. In England, King Henry I set up a collection of animals in about 1110 as part of the royal estate. His collection included tigers and lions. This collection eventually moved to the Tower of London in 1235. The collection stayed at that location for 600 years.

questions.prompt: How did Tariq make corn taste better?
options: By slapping some butter on it.
By enhancing its nourishment.
By growing it in South Dakota.
By cooking it in vegetable oil.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How did Tariq make corn taste better? 

 【翻译】 Tariq 是如何让玉米味道更好的? 
 A)  在玉米上涂一些黄油。 
 B)  通过增强其营养价值。 
 C)  通过在 South Dakota 种植它。 
 D)  通过用植物油烹饪它。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） By slapping some butter on it. 
 【定位】 P1 Everything changed for 7-year-old Tariq when he slapped some butter on an ear of corn. He knew it tasted good, but butter made it better. 
 对 7 岁的塔里克来说，当他往一根玉米上抹了点黄油时，一切都变了。他本就知道玉米好吃，但黄油让它更好吃了。 

 【信号】 but 后点出"黄油让它更好吃" 。答案句的信号是转折词 but：but butter made it better 直接把 butter 和 made it better 挂钩，正好回答"怎么让玉米更好吃"，转折之后的这半句才是落点。 

 【替换】 he slapped some butter on an ear of corn ↔ By slapping some butter on it. an ear of corn 被代词 it 概括 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音第2段确实提到玉米能 provides nourishment across the globe，B 项 By enhancing its nourishment. 盗用了 nourishment 这个原词，但那是讲玉米向全球提供营养，跟"塔里克怎么让玉米更好吃"无关，听到 nourishment 就选就中陷阱。  借用原文：The corn provides nourishment across the globe. 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 项 By growing it in South Dakota. 盗用了录音里的 South Dakota 这个高频地名，South Dakota is one of the top corn producers in America 说的是它是产玉米大州，与"让玉米更好吃"是两码事，属听到地名就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：South Dakota is one of the top corn producers in America. 

 D) 未提及 D 项 By cooking it in vegetable oil. 听起来也是个合理做法，且和正确项 A 的"加黄油"形成对立诱惑，但录音从头到尾只提了抹黄油，没说用植物油烹饪，属凭常识硬造、原文未提及。

questions.prompt: Why were Tariq and his family invited to South Dakota?
options: To introduce their corn to tourists.
To attend an honorary ceremony.
To share experience with other corn growers.
To exhibit their corn at the state's Corn Palace.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why were Tariq and his family invited to South Dakota? 

 【翻译】 为什么 Tariq 和他的家人被邀请到 South Dakota? 
 A)  向游客介绍他们的玉米。 
 B)  参加一个荣誉典礼。 
 C)  与其他玉米种植者分享经验。 
 D)  在该州的玉米宫展示他们的玉米。 

 【答案】 B （目的题） To attend an honorary ceremony. 
 【定位】 P2 Tariq and his family were invited to South Dakota to attend the honorary ceremony at the state's Corn Palace. 
 塔里克和他的家人受邀前往南达科他，去参加该州玉米宫举行的荣誉典礼。 

 【信号】 invited to… to attend… 把人和目的连起来 。答案信号是 invited 后接的目的不定式：were invited to South Dakota to attend the honorary ceremony，to attend 直接说明受邀目的就是参加荣誉典礼，这句一字对上题干所问。 

 【替换】 to attend the honorary ceremony ↔ To attend an honorary ceremony. the→an，去掉地点状语，核心动作不变 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 录音确实提到官方想突出 tourism and agriculture，A 项 To introduce their corn to tourists. 盗用了 tourism 引申出的 tourists，但那是官方的产业意图，不是塔里克一家"被邀请"的目的，二者主体不同，听到游客相关词就选会被带偏。  借用原文：Officials wanted to highlight South Dakota's two largest industries: tourism and agriculture. 

 C) 未提及 C 项 To share experience with other corn growers. 借 corn 这个全篇高频词造出"和其他玉米种植者交流经验"的合理场景，但录音通篇没说塔里克要去交流经验，属凭话题臆造、未提及。 
 D) 原词陷阱 D 项 To exhibit their corn at the state's Corn Palace. 盗用了答案句里真实出现的地名 at the state's Corn Palace，极具迷惑性；但录音说的是去玉米宫"参加典礼"，不是去那里"展出他们的玉米"，偷换了在玉米宫做的事，听到 Corn Palace 就选会中招。  借用原文：to attend the honorary ceremony at the state's Corn Palace

questions.prompt: What did Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman do according to a news release?
options: Stole mail several times.
Forged postal keys illegally.
Attacked postmen on multiple occasions.
Broke a number of postal collection boxes.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman do according to a news release? 

 【翻译】 根据一则新闻稿，Jordan Jax 和 Tarod Goodman 做了什么? 
 A)  多次盗窃邮件。 
 B)  非法伪造邮政钥匙。 
 C)  多次袭击邮递员。 
 D)  破坏了多个邮政收集箱。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Stole mail several times. 
 【定位】 P2 Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman, both 23, were arrested after evidence gathered in an investigation showed the pair stole mail on multiple occasions using a postal key, according to a news release. 
 据一份新闻稿，乔丹·贾克斯和塔罗德·古德曼，两人均为 23 岁，在一项调查所收集的证据显示二人多次盗窃邮件、并使用了一把邮政钥匙后，被逮捕。 

 【信号】 题干来源词回扣定位 。题干里的 according to a news release 与录音 according to a news release 逐字对应，这处来源短语就是定位信号：它出现的那一句正是承载答案的句子，紧接的 stole mail on multiple occasions 即两人所做之事。 

 【替换】 stole mail on multiple occasions ↔ Stole mail several times. 多次的同义改写 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音说两人 using a postal key，是使用一把邮政钥匙作案，并非 Forged postal keys illegally. 所说的非法伪造钥匙；选项盗用了 postal key 这一原词，却把使用偷换成伪造，答非所问。  借用原文：using a postal key 

 C) 张冠李戴 录音里的 on multiple occasions 修饰的是盗窃邮件，Attacked postmen on multiple occasions. 却把这个多次短语套到攻击邮递员上；录音通篇没有任何袭击邮差的内容，属盗用频次短语的张冠李戴。  借用原文：stole mail on multiple occasions 

 D) 原词陷阱 录音多处提到 collection boxes，如 collection boxes，但说的是两人用钥匙打开邮筒取信，从无砸坏之意；Broke a number of postal collection boxes. 盗用 collection boxes 原词，硬加上 Broke 这一录音没有的动作。  借用原文：collection boxes

questions.prompt: What do Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman face?
options: A sentence for life.
Loss of all their possessions.
Twenty-three years' hard labor.
Up to fifteen years in prison.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman face? 

 【翻译】 Jordan Jax 和 Tarod Goodman 面临什么? 
 A)  终身监禁。 
 B)  失去所有财产。 
 C)  二十三年苦役。 
 D)  最高十五年监禁。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Up to fifteen years in prison. 
 【定位】 P4 Jax and Goodman each face up to five years in federal prison in the mail thefts and up to ten years for possession of the postal key. 
 贾克斯和古德曼二人因盗窃邮件各面临最高五年的联邦监禁，并因持有邮政钥匙各面临最高十年监禁。 

 【信号】 题干动词 face 原句重现 。题干的 face 在录音 each face up to five years 里原样念出，这处动词回扣即定位信号；该句把两项刑期 up to five years 与 up to ten years 一并给出，正是答案所在。 

 【替换】 up to five years in federal prison ↔ Up to fifteen years in prison. 两项刑期相加得十五年 
 up to ten years for possession of the postal key ↔ Up to fifteen years in prison. 另一项刑期并入总数 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 录音只说面临有期的 five years 与 ten years，从未提无期；A sentence for life. 是夸大到终身监禁的后果，录音并无对应内容。 
 B) 未提及 录音谈的全是坐牢的年限，未提任何财产损失；Loss of all their possessions. 所说丧失全部财产在录音里毫无依据。 
 C) 原词陷阱 录音里的 23 出自两人年龄 both 23，并非刑期；Twenty-three years' hard labor. 盗用 23 这个数字，硬安成二十三年苦役，且 hard labor 录音也从未提及，把年龄数偷换成刑期。  借用原文：both 23

questions.prompt: Why has the clothing industry come under attack?
options: It escapes regulation and misleads consumers.
It ignores economically feasible recycling options.
It creates waste and severely impacts the environment.
It produces clothes affordable only to a tiny minority.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why has the clothing industry come under attack? 

 【翻译】 为什么服装行业受到抨击? 
 A)  它逃避监管并误导消费者。 
 B)  它忽视经济上可行的回收选择。 
 C)  它制造废物并严重影响环境。 
 D)  它生产的服装只有极少数人能够负担得起。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It creates waste and severely impacts the environment. 
 【定位】 P2 Recently, the clothing industry has come under attack for creating a waste problem with serious environmental consequences. 
 最近，服装业因制造废物问题、带来严重环境后果而受到抨击。 

 【信号】 题干原词 come under attack 复现处 。录音中 has come under attack for 与题干 come under attack 几乎一字不差，听到这个短语就锁定这句；紧跟 for 后面的内容正是被抨击的原因，即答案所在。 

 【替换】 creating a waste problem ↔ It creates waste 动名词转一般现在时 
 serious environmental consequences ↔ severely impacts the environment 名词短语改写成动词短语 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 说 misleads consumers（误导消费者），其中 consumers 是录音后文反复出现的原词，听到就想选；但录音说行业被抨击的原因是制造废物、害环境，从没说它误导消费者，A 借原词制造错觉。  借用原文：incentivize both manufacturers and consumers 

 B) 偷换概念 B 说 ignores economically feasible recycling options（忽视经济可行的回收方案），其中 recycling、economically feasible 直接来自录音 environmentally and economically feasible recycling options；但录音说的是这类回收方案本就缺失（in the absence of），不是行业故意忽视，B 把客观缺失偷换成主观无视。  借用原文：In the absence of environmentally and economically feasible recycling options 

 D) 与原文相反 D 说 produces clothes affordable only to a tiny minority（生产只有极少数人买得起的衣服），clothes、produces 是录音原词，但录音明说快时尚是 low-quality clothes produced in high volumes（低质、量产），价格便宜、人人能买，与 D 说的只有极少数人买得起恰好相反，录音也没提价格门槛。  借用原文：low-quality clothes produced in high volumes

questions.prompt: Why did the researchers put forth such policies as production tax?
options: To cut consumers' expenses in buying quality clothes.
To enable the whole fast-fashion industry to be sustainable.
To incentivize manufacturers to be more consumer-friendly.
To urge manufacturers and consumers to reduce waste.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why did the researchers put forth such policies as production tax? 

 【翻译】 为什么研究人员提出诸如生产税之类的政策? 
 A)  为了削减消费者购买优质服装的开支。 
 B)  为了使整个快时尚行业能够可持续发展。 
 C)  为了激励制造商更加关注消费者利益。 
 D)  为了敦促制造商和消费者减少废物。 

 【答案】 D （目的题） To urge manufacturers and consumers to reduce waste. 
 【定位】 P3 The researchers put forth policy contributions, ranging from sustainable disposal of leftover stock to production tax to incentivize both manufacturers and consumers to be more waste conscious. 
 研究者提出了一系列政策建议，从对剩余库存的可持续处理到征收生产税，目的是激励生产商和消费者都更有减废意识。 

 【信号】 目的状语 to incentivize 。录音里 to incentivize both manufacturers and consumers to be more waste conscious 是 production tax 后面的目的状语，to incentivize 就是表目的的信号，它后面的内容正是这些政策要达成的目标。 

 【替换】 incentivize both manufacturers and consumers ↔ urge manufacturers and consumers 同义动词替换 
 to be more waste conscious ↔ to reduce waste 概括式改写 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 说 cut consumers' expenses in buying quality clothes（替消费者省下买好衣服的钱），consumers 是录音原词，但录音讲政策目的是减废，从没说为消费者省钱，A 把减废目的偷换成省钱目的。  借用原文：incentivize both manufacturers and consumers 

 B) 过度推断 B 说 To enable the whole fast-fashion industry to be sustainable（让整个快时尚业可持续），sustainable 是录音开头出现的原词，但生产税这类政策的直接目的录音说得很具体——是激励双方减废，而非让整个行业可持续，B 把目的范围夸大了。  借用原文：Can fast-fashion be sustainable? 

 C) 偷换概念 C 说 incentivize manufacturers to be more consumer-friendly（激励生产商更体贴消费者），incentivize、manufacturers 是录音原词，但录音说的是激励双方更有减废意识，不是让生产商对消费者更友好，C 把减废目的偷换成讨好消费者。  借用原文：incentivize both manufacturers and consumers to be more waste conscious

questions.prompt: What should be done first to eliminate the harm caused by the clothing industry?
options: Recognizing the impact on consumers.
Identifying the source of the problem.
Abandoning the current business model.
Establishing powerful regulatory bodies.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What should be done first to eliminate the harm caused by the clothing industry? 

 【翻译】 要消除服装行业造成的危害,首先应该做什么? 
 A)  认识到对消费者的影响。 
 B)  找出问题的根源。 
 C)  放弃当前的商业模式。 
 D)  建立强有力的监管机构。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Identifying the source of the problem. 
 【定位】 P4 In order to devise effective policies to curb the environmental impact of the clothing industry, it is important to identify the source of the problem in the supply chain. 
 为了制定有效政策来遏制服装业对环境的影响，关键是先找出供应链中问题的根源。 

 【信号】 强调句 it is important to 。录音 it is important to identify the source of the problem 用 it is important to 强调首要之事，这就是表先后、表首要的信号词；它后面的动作 identify the source 即题目问的第一步。 

 【替换】 identify the source of the problem ↔ Identifying the source of the problem 动词原形转动名词，近乎原句 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 说 Recognizing the impact on consumers，其中 recognize、impact 来自录音 recognize the environmental impact of fast-fashion，听到就想选；但录音把这一步放在找出根源之后，而且说的是认识环境影响、不是对消费者的影响，既不是第一步、对象也被改了。  借用原文：recognize the environmental impact of fast-fashion 

 C) 过度推断 C 说 Abandoning the current business model（放弃现有商业模式），business model 取自录音 create new business models，但录音说的是创造新商业模式，从没说要放弃现有模式，C 把创造夸张成放弃。  借用原文：create new business models to manage waste 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 说 Establishing powerful regulatory bodies（建立强有力的监管机构），regulatory bodies 出现在录音 Manufacturers, consumers, and regulatory bodies 中，但录音只是提到监管机构是参与方之一，从没说要先建立强有力的监管机构，D 是凭原词编出来的。  借用原文：Manufacturers, consumers, and regulatory bodies can then take an informed approach

questions.prompt: Why is the woman complaining?
options: The city's rush-hour traffic is intolerable.
She cannot avoid rush-hour traffic.
The local government is inefficient.
The city is too big to move around easily.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why is the woman complaining? 

 【翻译】 女士为什么在抱怨? 
 A)  这座城市的高峰时段交通令人无法忍受。 
 B)  她无法避开高峰时段的交通。 
 C)  当地政府效率低下。 
 D)  这座城市太大了,出行不便。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） The city's rush-hour traffic is intolerable. 
 【定位】 P2 Rush hour in this city is killing me. 
 这座城市的高峰期真要把我折腾死了。 

 【信号】 她开口的第一句直接吐槽 。男方问"你怎么这么烦/出什么事了"之后，女方应答的第一句 Rush hour in this city is killing me. 就是直接吐槽，is killing me 这种强烈情绪用语正是抱怨的落点信号——被问者的第一反应往往就是答案句。 

 【替换】 Rush hour in this city is killing me. ↔ The city's rush-hour traffic is intolerable. is killing me 改写成 intolerable 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 盗用了录音里反复出现的 Rush hour 来勾人，但她抱怨的是高峰期"让人受不了"，从没说"她躲不开高峰"。She cannot avoid rush-hour traffic. 是凭空加上的内容，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：Rush hour is terrible 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音后面女方确实提到 the local government could help improve things，C 盗用"政府"这个原词，却编成"政府效率低"。她说的是"政府本可以帮忙改善"，并没说政府无能，C 答非所问。  借用原文：the local government could help improve things 

 D) 原词陷阱 男方说过 a city this big，D 盗用"城市大"这个原词，编成"城市太大不好出行"。但那是男方的话，且女方抱怨的对象是高峰期本身，不是城市大小，D 既张冠李戴又答非所问。  借用原文：a city this big

questions.prompt: What does the woman suggest doing?
options: Upgrading subway carriages.
Increasing the number of bus routes.
Air conditioning the city's subway.
Learning from other big cities.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman suggest doing? 

 【翻译】 女士建议做什么? 
 A)  升级地铁车厢。 
 B)  增加公交线路数量。 
 C)  为城市地铁安装空调。 
 D)  向其他大城市学习。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Air conditioning the city's subway. 
 【定位】 P6 Well, for example, the subway system could have air conditioning. I know many cities in the world have air conditioning in their subway, so why can't we? 
 比如说，地铁系统可以装空调嘛。我知道世界上很多城市的地铁都有空调，咱们为什么不能有呢？ 

 【信号】 建议信号 could 与 why can't we 。the subway system could have air conditioning 里的 could（可以…）就是建议信号，紧接着 why can't we（咱为什么不能）用反问加重了这条提议——could + 反问，正是"我建议这么做"的落点。 

 【替换】 the subway system could have air conditioning ↔ Air conditioning the city's subway. 句子改写成动名词短语 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 盗用录音里的 subway carriages（地铁车厢）来勾人。"车厢"确实念到了，但女方的建议是"装空调"，不是"升级车厢"。况且后面 The trains here are too old 是男方说的，不是女方的建议，A 答非所问。  借用原文：strangers packed close together in the subway carriages 

 B) 未提及 增开公交线路这件事女方从没提过。录音只在男方那段提到 Bus No. 36，与"增加线路"无关，B 属凭空捏造的措施。 
 D) 原词陷阱 D 盗用了 many cities in the world 里的"别的城市"来勾人，但女方提"很多城市有空调"是为论证"应给地铁装空调"，并非建议"向别的大城市学习"。D 把具体建议偷换成空泛口号，答非所问。  借用原文：I know many cities in the world have air conditioning in their subway

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
options: He suffers from rush-hour crowding too.
He is fortunate to live very near to work.
He takes a half-hour bus ride to work.
He is going to move closer to his office.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the man from the conversation? 

 【翻译】 从对话中我们了解到男士的什么情况? 
 A)  他也深受高峰时段拥挤之苦。 
 B)  他很幸运住得离工作地点非常近。 
 C)  他乘坐半小时公交车上班。 
 D)  他打算搬到离办公室更近的地方。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） He takes a half-hour bus ride to work. 
 【定位】 P9 Yeah, it's more convenient. Bus No. 36 goes straight from my house to the office. It's a 30-minute ride and I don't have to make any changes. 
 对，公交更方便。36 路车从我家直达办公室，车程 30 分钟，中途不用换乘。 

 【信号】 男方自述上班方式 + 数字 30-minute 。Bus No. 36 goes straight from my house to the office 是男方在讲自己怎么上班，紧跟的 It's a 30-minute ride 给出具体时长——"自述 + 数字"是细节题最硬的落点信号，听到数字就要立刻记下。 

 【替换】 It's a 30-minute ride ↔ He takes a half-hour bus ride to work. 30-minute 换说成 half-hour 
 Bus No. 36 goes straight from my house to the office ↔ bus ride to work 坐公交去办公室=坐公交上班 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 A 盗用录音里 rush-hour crowds 这个"高峰拥挤"原词来勾人，但受高峰挤之苦的是女方（坐地铁），男方说自己坐公交、还自称 fortunate。把女方的处境安到男方身上，是张冠李戴。  借用原文：the rush-hour crowds with strangers packed close together 

 B) 原词陷阱 B 盗用男方说的 I'm fortunate（我算幸运）来勾人。他幸运是因为"坐公交方便、不用挤地铁"，而不是"住得离公司很近"——通勤还要 30 分钟，谈不上很近。B 把"幸运的原因"偷换了。  借用原文：I guess I'm fortunate I take the bus instead 

 D) 张冠李戴 D 盗用了 move closer to the office 这个原词，但说"也许我该搬得离公司近点"的是女方，不是男方。把女方的打算记到男方头上，张冠李戴。  借用原文：Maybe I should move closer to the office

questions.prompt: What does the woman ask the man to do at the end of the conversation?
options: Recommend to her a good house near his office.
Send her his housing agent's telephone number.
Tell her exactly what kind of property to look for.
Make sure the agent finds something good for her.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman ask the man to do at the end of the conversation? 

 【翻译】 对话结束时女士要求男士做什么? 
 A)  向她推荐他办公室附近的好房子。 
 B)  把他的房产中介的电话号码发给她。 
 C)  准确告诉她应该寻找什么类型的房产。 
 D)  确保中介为她找到好房子。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Send her his housing agent's telephone number. 
 【定位】 P12 Hmm, could you send me his number, please? 
 嗯，你能把他的电话号码发给我吗？ 

 【信号】 请求句 could you…please 。could you send me his number, please? 用 could you…please 提出请求，正是"请对方做某事"的标准信号，且出现在对话末尾，与题干"at the end"对得上——这就是答案句。 

 【替换】 could you send me his number, please? ↔ Send her his housing agent's telephone number. his number 补全为中介的电话号码 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 盗用了对话里 move closer to the office、flat 这一带"房子"话题来勾人，但她请的是"发中介电话"，不是"请他直接推荐一套好房子"。把"给电话"偷换成"荐房"，答非所问。  借用原文：I found the flat I'm living in now through him 

 C) 张冠李戴 C 盗用了男方那句 tell him exactly what you are looking for，但那是男方让"她去告诉中介"要什么，不是她请男方做的事，也不是"由男方告诉她该找什么样的房"。既张冠李戴又把方向弄反。  借用原文：Just tell him exactly what you are looking for 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 盗用男方那句 he will find something good 来勾人，但那是男方对中介能办好的预期，不是女方请男方"确保中介给她找到好的"。把一句预期偷换成她的请求，答非所问。  借用原文：I'm sure he will find something good

questions.prompt: What does the man say about Johnny?
options: He was remembered for the scar on his cheek.
He received a heart operation a few days ago.
He used to wear a sad face in school.
He had some plastic surgery done.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say about Johnny? 

 【翻译】 男士对Johnny说了什么? 
 A)  他因脸颊上的疤痕而被人记住。 
 B)  他几天前接受了心脏手术。 
 C)  他在学校时常常一副悲伤的表情。 
 D)  他做了一些整形手术。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） He had some plastic surgery done. 
 【定位】 P3 He had some plastic surgery done. 
 他做了整形手术。 

 【信号】 对方一开口的核心信息 。男生在被问『他还好吗』之后，第一句给出的实质消息就是 He had some plastic surgery done.，这是整段对话的引子和核心事件，承载本题答案。 

 【替换】 He had some plastic surgery done. ↔ He had some plastic surgery done. 几乎原句照搬 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 He was remembered for the scar on his cheek. 借了录音里真出现过的 scar 和 cheek（女生说 I always remember him having that on his cheek），但那是女生说『记得他脸上有疤』，并非男生关于 Johnny 所说的核心事件；题问 the man 说了什么，答非所问。  借用原文：I always remember him having that on his cheek 

 B) 偷换概念 选项 He received a heart operation a few days ago. 蹭了录音里的 operation 一词（He had an operation done on it, plastic surgery），却擅自改成 heart operation（心脏手术）；录音说的是脸上的整形手术，不是心脏，属偷换。  借用原文：He had an operation done on it, plastic surgery 

 C) 未提及 选项 He used to wear a sad face in school. 里的 sad face（哭丧脸）录音根本没说，只是借了 school 一词（女生提到 I've known him since primary school）凑出来的；属无中生有。  借用原文：I've known him since primary school

questions.prompt: What does the woman find puzzling?
options: The man's deep sympathy for Johnny.
The man's use of the expression 'fixed'.
The man's covering up of what happened.
The man's good memory of his childhood.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman find puzzling? 

 【翻译】 女士觉得什么令人困惑? 
 A)  男士对Johnny的深切同情。 
 B)  男士使用"fixed"这个表达。 
 C)  男士对所发生事情的掩饰。 
 D)  男士对童年时光的良好记忆。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） The man's use of the expression 'fixed'. 
 【定位】 P8 Fixed? What do you mean? You can't fix a scar. 
 修好？你什么意思？疤是没法『修好』的。 

 【信号】 对某个用词的反问 。女生紧接男生说的 he had it fixed，立刻反问 Fixed? What do you mean? You can't fix a scar.——她重复并质疑了 fixed 这个词，反问语气正是『困惑』的信号，答案句就在此。 

 【替换】 Fixed? What do you mean? You can't fix a scar. ↔ The man's use of the expression 'fixed'. 把疑问句概括为『对用词不解』 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 选项 The man's deep sympathy for Johnny. 说男生对 Johnny 深表同情，录音里男生从头到尾没有表达同情，更不是女生困惑的点；属未提及。 
 C) 原词陷阱 选项 The man's covering up of what happened. 蹭了录音里 in order to cover it and make it less noticeable 的 cover，但原文 cover 是『遮盖那道疤』，选项偷换成『掩盖发生的事（隐瞒）』，且女生并不为此困惑。  借用原文：in order to cover it and make it less noticeable 

 D) 张冠李戴 选项 The man's good memory of his childhood. 里『好记性』其实是女生自己说的（I always remember him having that on his cheek），却被安到 the man 头上，且与『困惑』无关；属张冠李戴。  借用原文：I always remember him having that on his cheek

questions.prompt: What did the man think of Johnny's scar?
options: It gave him a noticeable smartness.
It made him appear even more manly.
It seemed to give him a certain uniqueness.
It seemed to make up for his physical defects.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the man think of Johnny's scar? 

 【翻译】 男士对Johnny的疤痕有何看法? 
 A)  它赋予了他明显的精明。 
 B)  它使他显得更加阳刚。 
 C)  它似乎赋予了他某种独特性。 
 D)  它似乎弥补了他的身体缺陷。 

 【答案】 C （态度观点题） It seemed to give him a certain uniqueness. 
 【定位】 P11 In fact, I thought it added character… like it gave him a certain uniqueness. 
 其实我觉得那道疤还添了几分个性……好像让他有种独特感。 

 【信号】 I thought 引出的主观评价 。男生用 In fact, I thought it added character… like it gave him a certain uniqueness，I thought 直接亮出他对疤的看法，且 In fact 加重了肯定语气，是承载态度的答案句。 

 【替换】 it gave him a certain uniqueness ↔ It seemed to give him a certain uniqueness. 近乎同句，只换了语气词 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 It gave him a noticeable smartness. 蹭了录音里多次出现的 noticeable（make it less noticeable），但 smartness（精明/帅气）男生从没说过；属用熟词拼凑的原词陷阱。  借用原文：make it less noticeable 

 B) 未提及 选项 It made him appear even more manly. 说疤让他更有男子气概，录音里男生评价用的是 character、uniqueness，从未说 manly；属未提及。 
 D) 与原文相反 选项 It seemed to make up for his physical defects. 蹭了录音 physical defects 一词，但男生说的是『有些缺陷确实丑、可 Johnny 的疤不是』，并不认为疤在弥补缺陷；这是反着用了原文，张冠李戴加曲解。  借用原文：I can understand some scars and physical defects can be ugly and distracting, but not Johnny's

questions.prompt: How could we describe the speakers' attitude towards Johnny's girlfriend?
options: Liberal.
Hostile.
Indifferent.
Critical.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How could we describe the speakers' attitude towards Johnny's girlfriend? 

 【翻译】 我们可以如何描述说话者对Johnny女友的态度? 
 A)  宽容的。 
 B)  敌对的。 
 C)  漠不关心的。 
 D)  批评的。 

 【答案】 D （态度观点题） Critical. 
 【定位】 P16 What? That's so superficial and selfish of her. If Johnny's girlfriend doesn't like him for who he is, then she does not deserve to be his girlfriend. 
 什么？她这么做也太肤浅、太自私了。如果 Johnny 的女友不能接受真实的他，那她就不配做他女友。 

 【信号】 连串贬义评价词 。女生对女友连用 so superficial and selfish（肤浅、自私）和 does not deserve（不配），都是强烈负面用词；加上男生附和 You are right，两人态度一致偏负面，这几句是态度答案句。 

 【替换】 That's so superficial and selfish of her ↔ Critical. 贬义评价归为『批评』 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 选项 Liberal.（开明、宽容）方向与录音相反——两人对女友是 superficial and selfish 的指责，毫无宽容之意；属与原文相反。  借用原文：That's so superficial and selfish of her 

 B) 过度推断 选项 Hostile.（充满敌意）程度太重，录音是批评女友的做法（肤浅、自私），并未到仇视、敌对的地步；属程度过度推断。 
 C) 与原文相反 选项 Indifferent.（漠不关心）与录音情绪冲突——女生说到激动处骂女友、还评 What a fool he is，明显在意、不是无所谓；属与原文相反。  借用原文：What a fool he is

questions.prompt: How did language come into being according to researchers?
options: Through deliberation.
Through evolution.
Through invention.
Through collaboration.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How did language come into being according to researchers? 

 【翻译】 根据研究人员的说法,语言是如何产生的? 
 A)  通过深思熟虑。 
 B)  通过进化。 
 C)  通过发明。 
 D)  通过协作。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Through evolution. 
 【定位】 P1 Researchers don't think language was invented; instead, they think it evolved. 
 研究者不认为语言是被发明出来的；相反，他们认为它是进化（演变）而来的。 

 【信号】 否定+instead 的对比落点 。这句靠 don't think 先否掉一个说法、再用 instead 引出真正的答案——『否定 + instead/but』之后才是真意。前半 language was invented（被发明）是要被排除的，后半 they think it evolved（进化而来）才是研究者的真实立场。 

 【替换】 they think it evolved ↔ Through evolution. 动词 evolved 名词化为 evolution 

 【排除】 C) 原词陷阱 Through invention. 直接套用了录音里的 invented 一词，听到 invent 就想选正中陷阱——但原文是 don't think language was invented，明确否定了『发明』这个说法，所以它恰恰是错的。  借用原文：Researchers don't think language was invented 

 A) 未提及 Through deliberation.（通过深思熟虑/商议）在录音里根本没出现，研究者只在 invented 和 evolved 之间表态，从未说语言是『商量出来的』。 
 D) 未提及 Through collaboration.（通过协作）听上去合理，但录音只谈『进化还是发明』，从没说语言是靠人们协作产生的，属于自己脑补、原文未给的内容。

questions.prompt: How did language start according to the first theory?
options: With people imitating sounds around them.
With people interacting with animals close by.
With people showing each other things nearby.
With people trying to string sounds together.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How did language start according to the first theory? 

 【翻译】 根据第一种理论,语言是如何起源的? 
 A)  人们模仿周围的声音。 
 B)  人们与附近的动物互动。 
 C)  人们相互展示附近的事物。 
 D)  人们试图将声音串联起来。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） With people imitating sounds around them. 
 【定位】 P2 The first theory is that language started with people making different sounds, mostly imitating the things around them, like animal calls, nature sounds, and the sounds of tools. 
 第一个理论是：语言始于人们发出各种不同的声音，主要是模仿周围的事物，比如动物的叫声、自然的声响和工具发出的声音。 

 【信号】 started with 直接点出起点 。这句用 language started with（语言始于……）这种明确的『起点』标志词，正面回答题干问的『怎么开始』；其后的 imitating the things around them（模仿周围事物）就是起步的具体动作。 

 【替换】 making different sounds, mostly imitating the things around them ↔ With people imitating sounds around them. imitating things around→imitating sounds around 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 With people interacting with animals close by. 抓住了录音里的 animal calls（动物叫声）做诱饵，但原文说的是『模仿动物的叫声』，不是『和身边的动物互动』——听到 animal 就选就掉进陷阱，模仿声音 ≠ 与动物互动。  借用原文：like animal calls, nature sounds, and the sounds of tools 

 D) 答非所问 With people trying to string sounds together. 套用了原文 stringing the words together，但那是录音明说『At some point』（在某个时间点）才出现的后期步骤，不是『怎么开始』；它答的是后来的事，与题干问的『起点』错位。  借用原文：people started stringing the words together to form sentences 

 C) 张冠李戴 With people showing each other things nearby. 的『互相展示身边的东西』其实更接近第三段第二个理论里的『比划、用手指东西』，而本题限定 the first theory，张冠李戴把另一个理论的内容搬了过来。  借用原文：pointing at things with their hands and imitating actions using their bodies

questions.prompt: Why did people switch from gesturing to making sounds according to the more recent theory?
options: Making sounds can free one's hands for doing other things.
Making sounds proves markedly easier than sign languages.
Making sounds enables one to express their ideas more explicitly.
Making sounds helps one communicate with people they can't see.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why did people switch from gesturing to making sounds according to the more recent theory? 

 【翻译】 根据较新的理论,人们为什么从做手势转向发出声音? 
 A)  发出声音可以解放双手去做其他事情。 
 B)  发出声音明显比手语更容易。 
 C)  发出声音使人能够更明确地表达自己的想法。 
 D)  发出声音有助于人们与看不见的人交流。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Making sounds helps one communicate with people they can't see. 
 【定位】 P3 The reason they switched to making sounds, the theory goes, is that talking out loud lets you communicate with someone even when you can't see them. 
 按这个理论的说法，人们之所以改用发声，原因是大声说话能让你即使在看不见对方的时候也能与之交流。 

 【信号】 The reason…is that 直给原因 。这句以 The reason they switched to making sounds 开头、用 is that 直接引出理由，是最明确的因果信号；is that 后面的 even when you can't see them 就是『为什么改成出声』的答案。 

 【替换】 communicate with someone even when you can't see them ↔ Making sounds helps one communicate with people they can't see. 几乎逐词对应的同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 过度推断 Making sounds can free one's hands for doing other things.『腾出双手做别的事』听上去很合理，但录音从手语切到发声时只给了『看不见也能交流』这一个理由，从没提过『腾出手』，这是凭常识自己补出来的，原文未给。 
 B) 原词陷阱 Making sounds proves markedly easier than sign languages. 借用了录音里的 sign language，但原文只说手语后来发展出发声，从没比较『出声比手语更容易』，这个 easier 的比较是凭空加上去的。  借用原文：after developing sign languages, people eventually started making sounds 

 C) 未提及 Making sounds enables one to express their ideas more explicitly.『能更清楚地表达想法』是个看似合理的好处，但录音给出的唯一理由是『看不见对方也能交流』，从没说出声能表达得『更明确』，属于无中生有。

questions.prompt: How would people describe someone who shows off their social status according to new research?
options: Well disciplined.
Quite confident.
Somewhat selfish.
Highly intelligent.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How would people describe someone who shows off their social status according to new research? 

 【翻译】 根据新研究,人们会如何描述炫耀自己社会地位的人? 
 A)  纪律严明的 
 B)  相当自信的 
 C)  有些自私的 
 D)  高度聪明的 

 【答案】 C （态度观点题） Somewhat selfish. 
 【定位】 P1 But new research found that people believe someone who shows off their social status cares more about benefiting themselves than helping others. 
 但新研究发现，人们认为炫耀自己社会地位的人更在意让自己得益，而非帮助他人。 

 【信号】 转折 But + new research 。答案句以 But new research found 起头，转折词 But 加上题干点名的『new research』双重信号——前一句讲『显得有钱被认为更聪明自律』是铺垫，But 之后才是新研究的真正结论，这正是答案落点。 

 【替换】 cares more about benefiting themselves than helping others ↔ Somewhat selfish. 整句释义→一词概括 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Well disciplined. 盗用了答案句前那句铺垫里的 disciplined，但那句说的是『显得有钱的人被认为更自律』，是 But 之前的对比信息，不是新研究对炫耀者的评价，听到 disciplined 就选正中陷阱。  借用原文：people who appear to be wealthy tend to be considered more intelligent, disciplined, and competent 

 B) 未提及 Quite confident.『相当自信』录音通篇没有提到，是凭『炫耀的人大概很自信』的常识硬推出来的，没有原文依据。 
 D) 原词陷阱 Highly intelligent. 盗用了铺垫句里的 intelligent，同样出自 But 之前『显得有钱者被认为更聪明』的对比信息，不是新研究对炫耀者的真正评价，与 A 是同一类陷阱。  借用原文：people who appear to be wealthy tend to be considered more intelligent

questions.prompt: When were participants more likely to choose someone who signaled their wealth or status?
options: When they wanted to have a competitive team member.
When they were looking for a cooperative workmate.
When they found collaboration essential to them.
When they were seeking someone to help them.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 When were participants more likely to choose someone who signaled their wealth or status? 

 【翻译】 参与者在什么情况下更可能选择那些展示自己财富或地位的人? 
 A)  当他们想要一个有竞争力的团队成员时 
 B)  当他们在寻找一个合作的工作伙伴时 
 C)  当他们发现合作对自己至关重要时 
 D)  当他们在寻找能帮助自己的人时 

 【答案】 A （细节题） When they wanted to have a competitive team member. 
 【定位】 P2 But participants were more likely to choose that person when they're looking for a competitive team member. 
 但当参与者在寻找一名有竞争力的团队成员时，他们更倾向于选这个人。 

 【信号】 转折 But + more likely 。本段先说『seeking cooperative members 时不太会选』，But participants were more likely to choose 用 But 转折并出现题干同款的 more likely to choose，这句把『更愿意选』明确配给了后面那种情形，正是答案句。 

 【替换】 looking for a competitive team member ↔ When they wanted to have a competitive team member. 近义动词替换 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 When they were looking for a cooperative workmate. 盗用了 looking for 的句式和『合作』概念，但录音说『找 cooperative members 时反而 less likely 选』，正好与题干问的 more likely 相反，是把『不选』的情形错当成『选』的情形。  借用原文：participants were less likely to choose someone who signals their wealth or status to join a group seeking cooperative members 

 C) 原词陷阱 When they found collaboration essential to them. 搬来第一段的 cooperation is essential 那层意思（collaboration、essential），听着很耳熟，但那是讲『需要合作时该谦逊』，与本题『更愿意选炫耀者』的情形无关，是典型听到熟词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：Modesty may be key when cooperation is essential 

 D) 未提及 When they were seeking someone to help them.『想找人帮忙时』录音从未把『更愿意选炫耀者』绑到这种情形上，是凭常识臆造的条件，无原文依据。

questions.prompt: What should people do when sharing their wealth and status online?
options: Avoid frightening competitors.
Make clear their social goal.
Adopt persuasive strategies.
Consider the consequences.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What should people do when sharing their wealth and status online? 

 【翻译】 人们在网上分享自己的财富和地位时应该做什么? 
 A)  避免吓到竞争对手 
 B)  明确自己的社交目标 
 C)  采用有说服力的策略 
 D)  考虑后果 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Consider the consequences. 
 【定位】 P3 People can easily share their wealth and status to large audiences, but they need to consider the consequences. 
 人们可以轻松地向广大受众展示自己的财富和地位，但他们需要考虑后果。 

 【信号】 建议信号 need to + 转折 but 。末段先说『社媒能轻易把财富地位分享给大众』，but they need to consider the consequences 用 but 转折并带 need to（需要做某事）这一建议信号，把『该怎么做』直接点出，是答案句。 

 【替换】 need to consider the consequences ↔ Consider the consequences. 建议句去主语即选项 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Avoid frightening competitors. 搬来末段的 frighten competitors，但录音说炫耀『可以帮你吓退竞争者』，那是分享地位的好处之一，并非『应该做什么』的建议；而且选项加了 Avoid（避免）把意思反成『避免吓退』，与原文方向不符。  借用原文：Posting about luxury purchases and expensive vacations online may help you to persuade others and frighten competitors 

 B) 张冠李戴 Make clear their social goal. 借了第二段的 depending on their social goal，但那句讲的是『按社交目标调整自我展示』，不是末段『网上分享该怎么做』的建议，是把别段内容安到本题头上。  借用原文：people should change how they present themselves depending on their social goal 

 C) 原词陷阱 Adopt persuasive strategies. 盗用末段 persuade others 的词根（persuasive），但录音说炫耀『可以帮你说服别人』也是好处之一，不是建议人去『采取说服策略』，属听到 persuade 就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：may help you to persuade others

questions.prompt: What can we see in the oldest cave paintings?
options: Much evidence of humans capturing animals.
More images of animals than humans.
Fewer images of buildings than animals.
Little proof of human fascination with animals.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What can we see in the oldest cave paintings? 

 【翻译】 我们能在最古老的洞穴壁画中看到什么? 
 A)  人类捕捉动物的大量证据。 
 B)  动物的图像多于人类的图像。 
 C)  建筑物的图像少于动物的图像。 
 D)  人类对动物着迷的证据很少。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） More images of animals than humans. 
 【定位】 P1 Of the oldest cave paintings discovered, some are up to 40,000 years old, and there are more images of animals than humans. 
 在已发现的最古老的洞穴壁画中，有些距今多达四万年，而且其中动物的图像比人类的图像更多。 

 【信号】 题干原词 oldest cave paintings 复现处 。原文 Of the oldest cave paintings discovered 与题干 the oldest cave paintings 是同一处，紧跟其后的 there are more images of animals than humans 就是承载答案的关键句，靠题干主题词在原文复现来定位。 

 【替换】 more images of animals than humans ↔ More images of animals than humans. 几乎原句照搬 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Much evidence of humans capturing animals. 盗用了下一句 humans began to capture and hold animals 的 capture 一词，但那讲的是后来人类开始圈养动物，不是壁画内容；题问壁画里能看到什么，答非所问。  借用原文：humans began to capture and hold animals 

 C) 未提及 Fewer images of buildings than animals. 里的 buildings 在第一段壁画的描述中根本没提（buildings 出现在第二段讲埃及建筑处），壁画只比较了 animals 与 humans，没说 buildings 的图像，属凭空捏造。 
 D) 与原文相反 Little proof of human fascination with animals. 用了开头句 Human fascination with animals 的原词，却说成 Little proof（很少证据）；而原文开头明说人类对动物的迷恋自古就有、壁画里动物图像还更多，恰恰是证据充分，极性完全相反。  借用原文：Human fascination with animals goes back as far as humans do

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the first-known collections of animals?
options: They were open to the public.
They were primarily native.
They were kept by royalty.
They were hardly injured.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the first-known collections of animals? 

 【翻译】 关于最早已知的动物收藏,我们了解到什么? 
 A)  它们向公众开放。 
 B)  它们主要是本地的。 
 C)  它们由皇室饲养。 
 D)  它们几乎没有受伤。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They were kept by royalty. 
 【定位】 P2 The first-known collections were held by royalty and were not open to the public. 
 已知最早的（动物）收藏由王室持有，并且不对公众开放。 

 【信号】 题干主语 first-known collections 在原文复现处 。原文 The first-known collections were held by royalty 与题干 the first-known collections of animals 是同一主语，紧跟其后对「归谁所有、是否开放」的正面陈述就是答案句，靠题干主语在原文复现来定位。 

 【替换】 were held by royalty ↔ They were kept by royalty. held 同义替换为 kept 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 They were open to the public. 借用了原文 not open to the public 里的 open to the public 短语，却把否定的 not 去掉，说成对公众开放；原文恰恰说这些最早的收藏不对公众开放，极性相反。  借用原文：were not open to the public 

 B) 与原文相反 They were primarily native. 盗用了原文 native 一词，却把意思整个说反：原文是 not native to Egypt（大象不是埃及本土的），选项却说 primarily native（主要是本土的），方向相反。  借用原文：which were not native to Egypt 

 D) 与原文相反 They were hardly injured. 借用了原文 injuries 一词，却说几乎没受伤；原文明说 their remains show evidence of severe injuries（遗骸显示有严重伤害），是伤得很重，与选项正好相反。  借用原文：their remains show evidence of severe injuries

questions.prompt: What might be the reason the Egyptian Queen created the zoo?
options: To enable the public to watch animals close by.
To introduce to Egyptians animals from Punt.
To protect the endangered animals.
To show off her riches and power.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What might be the reason the Egyptian Queen created the zoo? 

 【翻译】 埃及女王创建动物园的原因可能是什么? 
 A)  使公众能够近距离观看动物。 
 B)  向埃及人介绍来自Punt的动物。 
 C)  保护濒危动物。 
 D)  炫耀她的财富和权力。 

 【答案】 D （目的题） To show off her riches and power. 
 【定位】 P3 It's unclear why the Queen built the zoo, but it might have been to show off her wealth and power. 
 女王为何建这座动物园尚不清楚，但可能是为了炫耀她的财富与权力。 

 【信号】 转折 but 之后的目的句 。答案句的信号是转折加目的：It's unclear why 先说原因不明，转折词 but 之后 it might have been to show off her wealth and power 才给出真正的可能原因，but 后 + to do 处即答案。 

 【替换】 to show off her wealth and power ↔ To show off her riches and power. wealth 同义替换为 riches 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 To enable the public to watch animals close by. 把第三段开头 The first public exhibit of animals 里的 public 拿来当动机，但 public exhibit 只是给这座动物园定性，原文说的建园原因是炫耀财富权力，不是为让公众近距离看动物。  借用原文：The first public exhibit of animals 

 B) 张冠李戴 To introduce to Egyptians animals from Punt. 盗用了原文 a far-off land known as Punt 的地名 Punt，但原文说 Punt 只是动物的来源地（从那带回动物），不是建园是为了向埃及人介绍这些动物，张冠李戴。  借用原文：animals brought home from a far-off land known as Punt 

 C) 未提及 To protect the endangered animals. 说为保护濒危动物，但全文从未提到 protect 或 endangered，建园原因原文只给了炫耀财富权力一种，属凭空添加。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about King Henry I's collection of animals in England?
options: It was part of the royal estate.
It was a shelter for wild animals.
It was the kingdom's best-equipped zoo.
It was the first public exhibit of animals.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about King Henry I's collection of animals in England? 

 【翻译】 关于英格兰国王亨利一世的动物收藏,我们了解到什么? 
 A)  它是皇家庄园的一部分。 
 B)  它是野生动物的庇护所。 
 C)  它是王国中设备最齐全的动物园。 
 D)  它是第一个公开展出动物的地方。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It was part of the royal estate. 
 【定位】 P4 In England, King Henry I set up a collection of animals in about 1110 as part of the royal estate. 
 在英格兰，亨利一世国王约在 1110 年建立了一处动物收藏，作为王室领地的一部分。 

 【信号】 人名 King Henry I 后紧跟的定性 。定位靠人名复现：题干问 King Henry I，原文 In England, King Henry I set up a collection of animals 一出现这个名字，紧跟的 as part of the royal estate 就是对这处收藏的定性，即答案句。 

 【替换】 as part of the royal estate ↔ It was part of the royal estate. 近乎原句对应 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 It was a shelter for wild animals. 借用了全篇反复出现的 animals，但原文从没把亨利一世这处收藏说成野生动物的庇护所（shelter），这是凭空添加的定性。 
 C) 过度推断 It was the kingdom's best-equipped zoo. 用 best-equipped（装备最好的）拔高，但原文只说它是 part of the royal estate 并养有老虎狮子，从未评价它是王国里设施最好的动物园，属过度拔高。  借用原文：His collection included tigers and lions 

 D) 张冠李戴 It was the first public exhibit of animals. 盗用了第三段 The first public exhibit of animals 的原话，但那说的是埃及女王 Hatshepsut 的动物园，不是英格兰亨利一世这处，把别处的定性安到了这处头上。  借用原文：The first public exhibit of animals may have been created by Egypt's Queen Hatshepsut
